title: Easy to isolate, probably an anomaly
sub: One random isolation tree, followed down to a single point.

frames.caption: 64 points: a cloud of normal ones and one that sits apart (red). An isolation tree picks a random feature and a random cut between that feature's min and max, keeps the side containing our point, and repeats until the point is alone.
The first random cut. The green box is the region still containing the red point; blue points share it.
Cut 2: 4 points still share its box.

Alone after 3 cuts. A point far from the rest is easy to separate: a random cut has a good chance of falling in the empty space around it. Averaged over 500 random trees it takes 2.9 cuts, and its anomaly score is 0.76 (scores near 1 mean anomalous).
Now track a point in the middle of the cloud (red). Same procedure: random feature, random cut, keep its side.
The first cut removes a chunk of the cloud, but plenty of neighbours remain.
Cut 2: 29 points still share its box.
Cut 3: 25 points still share its box.
Cut 4: 22 points still share its box.
Cut 5: 19 points still share its box.
Cut 6: 16 points still share its box.
Cut 7: 12 points still share its box.
Cut 8: 11 points still share its box.
Cut 9: 6 points still share its box.
Cut 10: 3 points still share its box.

Alone only after 11 cuts: with neighbours all around, each cut peels off just a few of them. Averaged over 500 trees it takes 10.9 cuts (score 0.37, well below the outlier's 0.76). That gap in path length is the whole idea of Isolation Forest.
